components.note: 扌 (hand) — 掩 describes covering or shutting something with the hand.
奄 (yǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 掩.
扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'
钅 (metal) — early mirrors were made of polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) is an exact match for the sound of 镜.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.
The 曲-shaped top pictures a bundle of bamboo strips, an ancient book.
八 below pictures two hands supporting the book, giving 典 its meaning 'classic text, standard.'
氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.
图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'
⺺ — an abstract mark meant to depict strokes made by a writing brush, the origin of 书's meaning 'book, document, letter.'
饣 (food) points to a place where meals are served.
官 pictures an official hall or residence, giving 馆 its sense of a large public building.
日 (sun) — 显 relates to something bright and clearly visible in the light
业 (yè) gives a loose sound connection to 显's reading xiǎn
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'
匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'
开-shaped bars picture a cell or restraint.
刂 (knife) adds the idea of physical punishment, giving 刑 its meaning 'punishment, penalty.'
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'
辶 (to walk) — 追 relates to moving in pursuit of someone or something
㠯 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 追's reading zhuī, having drifted apart over time
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
A stylized drawing of orchid blossoms and leaves growing up from the ground.
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'
艹 (plant) — 苹 names a fruiting plant.
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 苹.
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'
Originally a pictograph of a musical bell or instrument hung in a frame; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional word 南, 'south.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
亻 (person) — 傻 describes a state of mind a person is in.
囟 (the top of the head), together with a striking motion below, pictures someone being hit on the head — the odd image behind 傻's meaning 'foolish.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
氵 (water) — 浴 relates to washing with water.
谷 (gǔ) gives a sound only distantly related to yù today, having drifted apart over time.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì
女 (woman) — 婚 relates to marriage, historically centered on the wife.
昏 (hūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婚.

meanings: short stories of the Tang and Song Dynasty

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a rider.
可 here is said to depict a mount — a person riding in an unusual way gave 奇 its meaning 'strange, odd, remarkable.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.

尹 (yǐn) gives a sound close to 伊's reading yī, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
止 depicts a footprint, with toes at the top and the leg below — a simple picture of a foot, later extended to mean 'to stop.'
页 (head) — 顾 originally related to turning the head to look back at something
厄 (è) gives a sound distantly related to 顾's reading gù, having drifted apart over time
口 (mouth) — 问 relates to speaking, specifically asking a question.
门 (mén) gives a hint of the sound — 问 is pronounced wèn, related but the tone and vowel have shifted.
阝 (mound, related to walls and terrain) — 障 describes something that blocks a path, like a wall.
章 (zhāng) gives a sound close to zhàng, differing only in tone.
石 (stone) — 碍 describes something solid, like a stone, blocking one's path.
㝵 gives a sound closely related to ài, though pronunciation has drifted somewhat over time.
厃 depicts a steep, overhanging cliff edge.
㔾 depicts a person crouching — together with 厃, the image of someone perched at a cliff's edge gave 危 its meaning 'dangerous.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
攵 (to act, strike) — 敏 describes being quick and effective in action, 'nimble, sharp.'
每 (měi) is only distantly related in sound to mǐn — the rhyme has drifted apart over time.
咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
十 (ten) — 博 relates to breadth, with ten symbolizing completeness.
尃 (fū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading bó has diverged considerably.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
饣 (food) points to a place where meals are served.
官 pictures an official hall or residence, giving 馆 its sense of a large public building.
冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
五 places an X-shaped cross between two horizontal lines representing heaven and earth — in traditional cosmology, this was linked to the five elements that fill the space between.
扌 (hand) — 摄 describes taking hold of or capturing something, as in taking a photograph.
聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to shè's reading, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.

A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.

尊 (to honor) shows respect for what is being followed, giving 遵 its meaning 'to obey, to comply with.'

A simplified pictograph of a bird's wings spread in flight — the source of 飞's meaning 'to fly.'
舟 (boat) — 船 is a vessel that travels on water, directly tied to its meaning 'ship, boat'
亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
